**Solution.**

Place the regular tetrahedron with vertices at four alternating corners of a cube of side length 2:

$$A=(1,1,1),\quad B=(1,-1,-1),\quad C=(-1,1,-1),\quad D=(-1,-1,1).$$

One checks that all pairwise distances equal $2\sqrt{2}$, so this is indeed a regular tetrahedron. Its center $O$ (the centroid, which coincides with the circumcenter) is the origin:

$$O=(0,0,0).$$

Thus

$$\vec{OA}=(1,1,1),\qquad \vec{OB}=(1,-1,-1),$$

with $|\vec{OA}|=|\vec{OB}|=\sqrt{3}$ and

$$\vec{OA}\cdot\vec{OB}=1\cdot 1+1\cdot(-1)+1\cdot(-1)=1-1-1=-1.$$

Hence

$$\cos(\angle AOB)=\frac{\vec{OA}\cdot\vec{OB}}{|\vec{OA}||\vec{OB}|}=\frac{-1}{3}.$$

Using $\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta-1=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta}-1$:

$$\tan^2(\angle AOB)=\frac{1}{(-1/3)^2}-1=\frac{1}{1/9}-1=9-1=8.$$

$$\boxed{\tan^2(\angle AOB)=8}.$$
